mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% over two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the rank information coefficient over triggered periods is not statistically significant at the 5% level.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the unemployment rate below 3.5% for three consecutive months indicates a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing corporate profit margins and resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during periods of simultaneous strong GDP growth.

mechanism_narrative: A sequential decline in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) for two consecutive months signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both decline for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the effect reverses when monetary policy is simultaneously expansionary.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) for three consecutive months signals a contraction in manufacturing activity, which reduces corporate earnings and capital expenditure, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO declines for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly different from zero during triggered episodes, or the effect is absent during periods of strong consumer demand growth.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp one-month increase in CPIAUCSL above 3.5% combined with a federal funds rate below 2% signals a surprise inflation shock with accommodative policy, which initially boosts market risk appetite and produces positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL > 3.5% AND FEDFUNDS < 2% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the effect is not statistically significant at the 5% level.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both payroll employment (PAYEMS) and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) in the same month signals a statistical artifact or data anomaly rather than genuine labor market strength, which historically has coincided with short-term S&P 500 volatility and negative 20-day returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases AND UNRATE increases in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the effect is not robust across multiple data vintages.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent annualized GDP growth rate (GDPC1) above 4% for four consecutive quarters signals a strong economic expansion, which supports higher corporate earnings and risk appetite, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 > 4% annualized for four consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly above zero during triggered periods, or the effect reverses during periods of high inflation.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous two-month decline in both real personal savings (RSAFS) and housing starts (HOUST) indicates reduced household liquidity and construction activity, which signals weaker future consumption and investment, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS and HOUST both decline for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 45% of triggered episodes, or the effect is not statistically significant during periods of strong credit growth.
